topic: Infinite Beauty: Holomorphic Dynamics and Iterated Complex Functions
target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students with a basic interest in calculus and complex numbers

sections.title: The Concept of an 'Infinite Loop'
lecture_lines: Iteration feeds a function's output back as input.
This creates a sequence called an orbit.
Points can explode to infinity or shrink away.
animations: Highlight 'Feedback Loop' text (#FFFFFF) and create a circular arrow loop in the center.
Animate a green dot (#00FF00) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/dot.svg] jumping on a number line from 2 to 4 to 16 and then off-screen right.
Animate a green dot (#00FF00) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/dot.svg] on a number line jumping from 0.5 to 0.25 to 0.0625, approaching the origin.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The 2D Playground (Complex Plane)
lecture_lines: Complex numbers live on a 2D plane.
Squaring a number stretches its distance from zero.
This operation also rotates the point around the origin.
animations: Fade in a 2D coordinate plane with 'Re' and 'Im' axis labels (#FFFFFF).
Create a cyan vector (#00FFFF) from (0,0) to (1,1); rotate it 45 degrees and stretch it to (0,2).
Show multiple points with distinct colors (#FF00FF, #FFFF00) moving in unique curved paths across the plane.

sections.title: The Core Equation: f(z) = z² + c
lecture_lines: The dynamic begins with the formula z squared plus c.
Here, c acts as a constant shift or nudge.
Squaring rotates and stretches our current position.
Adding c pushes the point in a new direction.
This repeated process generates a complex path or orbit.
animations: Fade in the equation 'f(z) = z^2 + c' centered on screen in white (#FFFFFF).
Place a blue SurroundingRectangle (#0000FF) around the variable 'z' to highlight it as the position.
Place a red SurroundingRectangle (#FF0000) around the constant 'c' to highlight it as the nudge.
Sequentially display the text 'z0 -> z1 -> z2' with white arrows (#FFFFFF) appearing between them.
Wait 2.0s, then show a green point (#00FF00) making a series of jumps based on the equation.

sections.title: Stability vs. Chaos: Fatou and Julia Sets
lecture_lines: Predictable orbits belong to the stable Fatou set.
Other points escape to infinity in chaotic paths.
The boundary between stability and chaos is the Julia set.
These boundaries are infinitely complex and jagged.
Small changes on this edge lead to massive shifts.
animations: Fade in a solid blue region (#0000FF) representing the stable 'Fatou Set'.
Draw a complex, jagged white outline (#FFFFFF) around the blue region to represent the 'Julia Set'.
Show two nearby points (#00FF00 and #FF0000); one stays in the blue, the other exits the screen quickly.
Use a morphing transformation to transition the jagged Julia boundary into a smooth shoreline (#FFFF00) and back.
Perform a 3-second 'smooth' zoom into a small section of the Julia Set boundary to reveal detail.

sections.title: The Map of All Maps: The Mandelbrot Set
lecture_lines: Each value of c creates a unique Julia set.
The Mandelbrot set maps these different c values.
If an orbit stays bounded, we color it black.
Moving across the map morphs the Julia set's shape.
It is the ultimate dictionary of complex dynamics.
animations: Pop up several miniature Julia Set icons (#FFFFFF) in a circle around the center of the screen.
Fade in the large, iconic silhouette of the Mandelbrot Set with a white outline (#FFFFFF).
Show a red point 'c' (#FF0000) moving; as it moves, a side-window shows the Julia Set shape changing.
Fill the interior of the Mandelbrot Set silhouette with solid black (#000000).
Wait 1.5s, then display the title 'The Mandelbrot Set' in gold (#FFD700) with a brief flash effect.

sections.title: Summary: Complexity from Simplicity
lecture_lines: A simple rule generates infinite fractal beauty.
Small patterns mirror the structure of the whole.
Complex dynamics reveal the order within chaos.
animations: Grow a green fractal tree (#00FF00) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tree.svg] starting from a single trunk, branching out recursively.
Perform a 4-second 'smooth' zoom into a branch of the tree to show it looks identical to the whole tree.
Display the equation 'z = z^2 + c' (#FFFFFF) and animate it scaling up and down slowly to emphasize its power.
